subject: Novus order form - IP allocation, training opt-out & runtime safeguards
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novus order form - IP allocation, training opt-out & runtime safeguards

Elaine / team,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. I skimmed the redlines and flagged three items that will affect both the legal approval path and our operations plan:

- Output ownership / "derivative" wording — your redline narrows our ability to use aggregated telemetry; we'd like to suggest language that preserves customer output ownership while allowing Redwood to improve the service without exposing customer-specific outputs.
- Training opt-out scope — procurement's mark removes our right to include customer prompts in any retrain. We can accommodate a strict opt-out but need a clear operational signal (non-retraining flag + audit trail) and evidence requests to verify exclusion.
- Feedback license & telemetry — you removed the feedback license; our platform relies on telemetry for model monitoring and safety fixes. We propose a limited, aggregated telemetry license that excludes raw prompts and PII.

Can Laura + Ben weigh in on minimum language and the operational controls we'd need to satisfy procurement? I'm attaching the redlines you sent and we can propose counter-language. Goal is to have a short legal + ops playbook so procurement can close quickly.

Attachments: Novus_OrderForm_redlines.pdf (from Novus)

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference | +1-415-555-0132

Subject: Re: Novus order form - IP allocation, training opt-out & runtime safeguards

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick read. Attached is the version procurement redlined this morning (same file you have but I added a comment in the training opt-out clause). Our major asks are:

1) Customer retains all output rights and derivative title. We expect a hard opt-out for retraining — that should be reflected in the order form (not just policy).
2) No use of customer prompts for model retraining unless explicitly consented via an added order form exhibit.
3) We cannot accept a broad telemetry license that allows persistent retention of raw prompts. Aggregated telemetry for performance metrics is ok.

We understand there are operational implications — please provide the exact controls Redwood will implement (audit logs, retention windows, non-retraining flag, evidence for exclusions). Procurement needs those for their security/compliance review.

Attached: Novus_OrderForm_redlines.pdf (annotated)

Thanks,
Elaine Park

Jordan / Ben —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed Novus' redlines and drafted concise counter-language and an evidence checklist. I attached an annotated Word with tracked changes (jordan_legal_annotated_redlines.docx). Summary below — this is designed to be procurement-friendly while preserving Redwood's ability to operate and improve the service.

Proposed order-form clauses (short):
1) Output ownership: "Customer owns Outputs produced by Redwood in response to Customer Input under this Order Form. Redwood does not assert ownership of Customers' Outputs and shall not use Outputs to identify Customer."

2) Training opt-out: "Customer may elect an explicit 'Non-Retrain' flag at the Account/Order level. While this flag is in effect, Customer Input and corresponding Outputs will be excluded from datasets used to train or fine-tune Redwood models. Redwood will implement and maintain operational controls to honor this flag and shall provide an audit log demonstrating exclusion upon reasonable request."

3) Telemetry / Feedback license (narrow): "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and metrics derived from Customer interactions for the purposes of service monitoring, safety fixes, model quality improvements, and debugging, provided that such telemetry does not contain raw Customer Input or Outputs, and Redwood will not retain raw Customer Input beyond the retention window defined in Exhibit B."

Evidence checklist for procurement:
- SOC 2 report and scope statement (current).
- Data flow diagram showing how Customer Input is processed, cached, and purged.
- Description of the 'Non-Retrain' flag implementation (how it's recorded, how it's enforced at training pipeline level).
- Audit log sample demonstrating exclusion for a mock account.
- Retention policy for raw prompts and a proposed retention window (e.g., 7 days for KV cache; 30 days for debug logs, subject to redaction).

Risks if we accept a "hard opt-out" without operational controls: procurement could demand permanent deletion of signals that we rely on for safety/regression detection, increasing model risk. The order-form language above aims to give Novus certainty while preserving our ability to operate safely.

I recommend we send Novus the three clause counters + the evidence checklist. If they accept, we'll prepare Exhibit B with concrete retention numbers and the DocuSign amendment.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.inference

Subject: Re: Novus order form - IP allocation, training opt-out & runtime safeguards

Quick operational notes to pair with Laura's language — these are the controls engineering needs to satisfy procurement without blocking the deal: 

- Non-Retrain flag: implement as an account-level boolean persisted in our control plane. Training pipelines must consult the control plane and ignore flagged accounts; we will add a monotonic audit entry for each training run describing which account buckets were excluded.
- KV cache & prefixes: ensure customer-specific KV caches are ephemeral (TTL <= 7 days) and provide config to disable prefix caching for flagged accounts.
- Telemetry: emit only aggregated metrics (latency, token rates, failure counts) to analytics; raw logs must be redacted automatically before longer-term storage.
- Model variant fallback: offer a variant that is pipeline-isolated (no telemetry copy) for customers with strict needs; this may incur higher cost and slight latency.
- Operational SLAs: provide a one-page runbook for procurement showing enforcement steps, roles (engineering, infra, legal), and a timeline for audit evidence (we can produce a redacted sample within 3 business days once countersigned).

If procurement accepts the above, engineering can deliver the audit sample and DocuSign exhibit. Possible cost/latency delta for a variant will be presented in a short note for procurement to accept or decline.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference
